stages.name: Loyal Egyptian vassal
stages.desc: City-kings who swore loyalty to Pharaoh and wrote to him for help

stages.name: Held by Amurru
stages.desc: Cities taken by Abdi-Ashirta, Aziru and their allies

stages.name: Hittite sphere
stages.desc: Hatti and the kings who swore oaths to Suppiluliuma

stages.name: Mitanni
stages.desc: The Hurrian kingdom of Mitanni and its Syrian vassals

stages.name: Egyptian garrison or province
stages.desc: Egypt itself and its bases: Gaza, Kumidi, Sumur, Beth-Shean

states.name: Israel
timeline: Megiddo, Akko and Hazor are vassal cities; Egypt keeps a garrison at Beth-Shean
Biridiya of Megiddo resists Lab'ayu of Shechem, who is captured and killed

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Gaza is Egypt's main base in Canaan; the hill country is ruled by city-kings
Lab'ayu of Shechem raids his neighbours in the hills
Abdi-Heba of Jerusalem warns that the 'Apiru are taking the king's land

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Byblos, Beirut, Sidon and Tyre are loyal vassals; Egypt garrisons Kumidi in the Beqaa
Abdi-Ashirta of Amurru seizes Batruna and the towns north of Byblos
Zimredda of Sidon sides with Aziru and besieges Tyre
Rib-Hadda is driven from Byblos; Amurru and Sidon dominate the coast
Amurru, now a Hittite vassal, holds the north; Tyre and Byblos stay nominally Egyptian

states.name: Syria
timeline: Mitanni is overlord of northern Syria; Egypt holds Sumur and the south
Aziru takes Sumur, Egypt's base on the coast
Suppiluliuma's One-Year War: Mitanni's Syrian vassals fall to the Hittites
Aziru of Amurru swears a treaty with Suppiluliuma

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Hatti, in central Anatolia, recovers from invasions on every side
Suppiluliuma I takes the throne at Hattusa

states.name: Jordan
timeline: Pella and the Jordan valley towns are ruled by vassal kings
Mut-Ba'lu of Pella writes to Pharaoh protesting his loyalty

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Amenhotep III rules from Thebes at the height of Egypt's wealth and power
Amenhotep IV, soon Akhenaten, succeeds his father
Akhenaten founds a new capital, Akhetaten, at Amarna; the foreign letters follow him there
Akhenaten dies; a short, obscure succession follows
Tutankhamun returns the court to Thebes and Memphis; Amarna is abandoned

events.title: Letters of great kings
events.text: Pharaoh's court exchanges clay-tablet letters in Akkadian with Babylon, Mitanni, Hatti and Alashiya.

events.title: A Mitannian bride
events.text: Tushratta of Mitanni sends his daughter Tadukhipa to marry Amenhotep III, and asks for gold in return.

events.title: Abdi-Ashirta rises
events.text: Abdi-Ashirta, a warlord of the Amurru hills, gathers 'Apiru bands and claims to guard Sumur for Pharaoh.

events.title: Rib-Hadda's first pleas
events.text: The king of Byblos begins the longest correspondence in the archive, asking for archers.

events.title: Ammiya kills its lord
events.text: The people of Ammiya murder their king and join Abdi-Ashirta; Rib-Hadda writes that he is afraid.

events.title: Batruna falls
events.text: Abdi-Ashirta takes Batruna, a day's march from Byblos.

events.title: Irqata's king murdered
events.text: Aduna, king of Irqata, is killed; the city's elders write to Pharaoh on their own.

events.title: A widowed field
events.text: Rib-Hadda writes that his fields, unploughed for want of men, are like a woman without a husband.

events.title: Akhenaten's accession
events.text: Amenhotep III dies; his son Amenhotep IV, later Akhenaten, inherits the letters and the crisis.

events.title: Kumidi garrison
events.text: Egypt's base at Kumidi in the Beqaa watches the inland road to Damascus.

events.title: Abdi-Ashirta dies
events.text: Rib-Hadda reports that Abdi-Ashirta is dead, perhaps killed after an Egyptian expedition.

events.title: Suppiluliuma crowned
events.text: A young prince seizes the Hittite throne at Hattusa and begins rebuilding the kingdom.

events.title: Lab'ayu killed
events.text: The rebel king of Shechem is captured by his neighbours and killed before he can be sent to Pharaoh.

events.title: The sons return
events.text: Aziru and his brothers take back their father's towns and close in on Sumur.

events.title: Trapped in Byblos
events.text: Rib-Hadda writes that he is shut in Byblos like a bird in a trap.

events.title: A hymn from Tyre
events.text: Abimilku of Tyre greets Pharaoh as the sun that rises over the lands, in a letter shaped like a hymn.

events.title: Akhetaten founded
events.text: Akhenaten marks out a new capital at Amarna; a records office there keeps the foreign letters.

events.title: Beirut seizes ships
events.text: The king of Beirut confiscates two Byblian merchant ships, Rib-Hadda complains.

events.title: Sumur falls
events.text: Aziru takes Sumur, Egypt's administrative centre on the northern coast.

events.title: Zimredda turns
events.text: Zimredda of Sidon joins Aziru and blockades his rival, Tyre.

events.title: Jerusalem's warnings
events.text: Abdi-Heba of Jerusalem writes that the king's land is lost to the 'Apiru.

events.title: Gaza
events.text: Egypt's commissioners and troops gather at Gaza, the gateway to Canaan.

events.title: Neither water nor wood
events.text: Abimilku writes that island Tyre has neither water to drink nor wood to keep warm.

events.title: Ugarit's palace burns
events.text: Abimilku reports that fire has destroyed half the palace of the king of Ugarit.

events.title: Qatna warns
events.text: Akizzi of Qatna tells Pharaoh that Hittite troops are moving south, with Aitakkama of Qadesh.

events.title: Washukanni sacked
events.text: In a single campaign Suppiluliuma crosses the Euphrates and plunders the capital of Mitanni.

events.title: Aleppo and Alalakh
events.text: Mitanni's western vassals, Aleppo and Alalakh among them, pass to the Hittites.

events.title: Qadesh falls
events.text: Suppiluliuma defeats Shutatarra of Qadesh; his son Aitakkama becomes a Hittite vassal.

events.title: Ugarit submits
events.text: Niqmaddu II of Ugarit recognises Suppiluliuma as his overlord.

events.title: Exile in Beirut
events.text: Rib-Hadda goes to Beirut to seek an alliance with its king, Ammunira.

events.title: The gates are shut
events.text: While he is away, his brother Ilirabih seizes Byblos and bars him from his own city.

events.title: Handed to Sidon
events.text: Abandoned by Egypt, Rib-Hadda turns to Aziru, who hands him over to the kings of Sidon.

events.title: Hittites in Amki
events.text: Hittite raiders strike the Amki plain in the Beqaa, Egyptian-held land.

events.title: Pharaoh's summons
events.text: Akhenaten writes to Aziru, accusing him of disloyalty and ordering him to Egypt.

events.title: Aziru detained
events.text: Aziru is held at Pharaoh's court for about a year, while rumours say he will never return.

events.title: Hittites in Nuhasse
events.text: Aziru's brothers write that Hittite troops in Nuhasse threaten Amurru; Pharaoh lets Aziru go.

events.title: Aziru's treaty
events.text: Back home, Aziru swears loyalty to Suppiluliuma; Amurru will stay Hittite for over a century.

events.title: Akhenaten dies
events.text: The king who received most of Rib-Hadda's letters dies at Amarna.

events.title: Tushratta murdered
events.text: The king of Mitanni is killed by one of his sons; his kingdom breaks apart.

events.title: Amarna abandoned
events.text: Tutankhamun's court leaves Amarna; the letters stay behind in the ruins.

events.title: Carchemish holds out
events.text: Mitanni's last Syrian stronghold on the Euphrates resists the Hittites, until a later siege.

chartNote: Share of the area of seven present-day countries, by the power that dominated most of each one; regions are today's boundaries. The Late Bronze Age Levant was a patchwork of small city-states, so this is a simplification: in Lebanon, Tyre and Byblos stayed nominally Egyptian while Amurru held the north. Dates are BC and approximate.
